name: Bass music - 140 half-time arrangement map
description: Lays named section locators for a 140 BPM half-time bass track: intro, build, three eight-bar drop blocks, break, second build, second drop and outro. One reversible write with a dry-run preview; move or trim the markers afterwards with sections_move. Drop blocks are eight bars so the map fits the compact structure the style guides describe, not the 32-bar radio form.

steps.why: Name the eight-bar blocks so 'make the second drop heavier' has a target the tools can address.

manual.instruction: Clear or move any locator already sitting on these bars before applying; sections_create_locators refuses an occupied bar rather than replacing a marker. Save the Set first so the scratch copy has something to recover.
manual.verify: The dry-run shows nine markers created and none refused.
manual.why: The handler refuses occupied destinations, and the anchor Set must exist before the first applied write.

manual.instruction: For riddim, keep drops to one or two eight-bar loops and repeat the same motif; the drop blocks can be shortened and the second drop made a variation rather than a new part.
manual.verify: The riddim drop repeats one motif instead of introducing a new bassline per block.
manual.why: Riddim is defined by a single short motif repeated; the block map is a container, not a reason to change the riff.

manual.instruction: For tearout, make DROP 1B and DROP 2 the loudest, most layered blocks and use the last bar of each build for a siren or riser. Deathstep usually wants a longer, quieter intro and blast-beat kick fills at the eight-bar seams.
manual.verify: The loudest block is the second drop, and the builds have a transition, not just a filter sweep.
manual.why: Both styles build tension by contrast: a quieter build makes the drop read as heavier.

manual.instruction: Move the markers to match the actual material rather than moving the music to the markers. sections_move is the reversible way to do it, and the before/after is visible in sections_map.
manual.verify: sections_map lists the sections where the clips actually change.
manual.why: Locators that do not line up with the arrangement make every later structural tool act on the wrong bars.

notes: Sources: EDMProd's eight-bar UK dubstep structure (https://www.edmprod.com/how-to-make-dubstep); KAN Samples' longer 32/16-bar arrangement map (https://kansamples.com/blogs/learn/dubstep-track-arrangement); Melodigging's deathstep and tearout genre notes for the per-style differences (https://www.melodigging.com/genre/deathstep, https://www.melodigging.com/genre/tearout). The two arrangement guides disagree on block length; this map uses the compact one and says so. Executable through the normal plan path: dry-run, scratch copy, locator rollback.
